title: Scalar reverse maps on affine inverse limits
statement: For the affine section map of coherent formal modules, every pair of scalars in K(U)^t admits a linear reverse map on inverse limits whose two composites are multiplication by their product.

proof.text: At each level coherence implies quasi-coherence on the Noetherian scheme. Kernels and cokernels of the component maps are quasi-coherent.

Apply the ideal-power vanishing criterion to the cover of all affine opens, first to the kernel and then to the cokernel. Sections of the kernel map onto the linear kernel (range_map_kernelι), so linearity transfers annihilation. The affine cokernel linear equivalence transfers annihilation from the categorical cokernel sections to the quotient by the component map range.

For fixed f,g in K(U)^t, apply the scalar quasi-inverse theorem at every level. Choose the reverse maps with their lifting formula; the formula uniquely determines each map since lifts exist. The naturality clause of the same theorem, applied to the naturality square of alpha, makes these maps a natural transformation from the G-section diagram to the F-section diagram.

Apply lim.map to the reverse natural transformation. For both composite identities apply limit.hom_ext: limMap_π moves the composite through each projection, and the termwise scalar identity and linearity of the projection give multiplication by f*g. Apply ModuleCat.Hom.hom to recover the stated linear-map identities. This is the proved private limit_scalar_composites helper.

proof_origin.place: Remark 0888, final paragraph; affine-section transport supplied by the cited library lemmas

theorem coherentFormalModule_affine_limit_scalar_composites
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (I K : X.IdealSheafData)
    (F G : CoherentFormalModule X I) (α : F ⟶ G) (t : ℕ) (ht : 1 ≤ t)
    (h : ∀ n : ℕ,
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2
        (kernel (α.hom.app (op n)))) ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2
        (cokernel (α.hom.app (op n))))) (U : X.affineOpens) :
    ∀ (f g : Γ(X, U.1)), f ∈ K.ideal U ^ t → g ∈ K.ideal U ^ t →
      ∃ k : affineLimitModule X I G U →ₗ[Γ(X, U.1)] affineLimitModule X I F U,
        k.comp (lim.map (Functor.whiskerRight α.hom
          (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op U.1)))).hom =
          (f * g) • (LinearMap.id : affineLimitModule X I F U →ₗ[Γ(X, U.1)]
            affineLimitModule X I F U) ∧
        (lim.map (Functor.whiskerRight α.hom
          (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op U.1)))).hom.comp k =
          (f * g) • (LinearMap.id : affineLimitModule X I G U →ₗ[Γ(X, U.1)]
            affineLimitModule X I G U)
